task.description:
WF-03 Step 3d -- IDIOM/INTEGRITY GATE on the ISS-0109 implementation. Review the DIFF:
`git diff 70736d5..HEAD -- test/` (the new helper test/support/tenant_fixture.ex plus its adoption
in test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs).

SECURITY-REVIEWER has already PASSed this diff (step-03c) with per-invariant verdicts, and
verified INV-F-8 query-by-query and INV-F-9 interpolation-site-by-site. Do not redo that work.

Your standard scope applies: idiomatic Elixir/OTP usage, supervision integrity, scope creep,
decision-record consistency. The gate-approved design is lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md (passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR
at bf87afb, plus two ORCH label corrections at 4a20f7a).

FOUR SPECIFIC THINGS THIS RUN NEEDS YOU TO RULE ON. Three are ELIXIR-DEV's own flagged MINORs
where it deliberately did NOT decide unilaterally; the fourth is scope.

RULING 1 (the important one) -- A REAL INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN THE GATE-APPROVED DESIGN,
which neither CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR pass caught. SS3.2 types registration_present? and
schema_present? as boolean(). SS3.5 -- which INV-F-4 explicitly names as normative for
capture_schema_state/1's failure boundary -- requires a scalar whose query failed to degrade to
nil. Both cannot hold. ELIXIR-DEV implemented SS3.5 (boolean() | nil, where false means
observed-absent and nil means not-observed) and documented it in the moduledoc. Rule on this
explicitly: is implementing the normative section the right resolution, and is the resulting
@type/@spec surface coherent? Note the substantive argument in favour, and check it rather than
accept it: taking SS3.2's literal boolean() would report an UNOBSERVED schema as ABSENT, which is
precisely the observed-vs-unobserved conflation SS3.5 exists to forbid, and a capture report that
says "schema absent" when it simply failed to look would be worse than no report -- it would have
re-created ISS-0109's original misdiagnosis in a new place. If you agree, say so and ORCH will
have the design's SS3.2 corrected to match. If you disagree, this is a FAIL and the code changes
instead.

RULING 2 -- SS3.6 asks the teardown line to carry the owning test module/name, but the normative
five-key opts carry no ExUnit context and ExUnit exposes no public "current test" API (it lives
under the ExUnit.Runner key in the module-runner process's dictionary, not the test process's).
ELIXIR-DEV's owning_test/0 walks the OTP-25+ :parent chain, the same shape as ExUnit's own
safe_pdict_current/1, and degrades to "unknown" rather than ever failing a teardown. Rule on
whether reaching into another process's dictionary via the :parent chain is acceptable idiom HERE
(test-only helper, best-effort log enrichment, degrades safely) or whether it is the kind of
private-internals coupling that will silently break on an ExUnit change. If the latter, say what
the code should do instead -- note that the marker, the phase and schema_present_before_drop do
NOT depend on it, so dropping the field entirely is an available answer.

RULING 3 -- tables_present deliberately excludes schema_migrations (its contents are captured
separately as applied_versions), matching expected_tenant_tables/0, so SS3.3's oracle-rot test
stays a plain both-direction set equality with no filtering on TEST-DESIGNER's side. Confirm this
is consistent and that the oracle-rot guard specified in the design still works against the
implementation as written.

RULING 4 -- SCOPE. Confirm the diff does not creep beyond the design: exactly one new test-only
module, adoption in exactly the two modules ISS-0109 names, no touch to the other 39 copy-paste
sites (ISS-0112/GH#366), no production change (INV-F-2), drop_schema!/1 still present in
promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs for its unrelated SandboxPool caller at :463. Also confirm the
helper does not quietly absorb any of ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113 or ISS-0107.

ALSO CHECK, as ordinary idiom review of a 630-line new module: naming, @spec accuracy against
actual return shapes, the guarded/rescue structure (SECURITY-REVIEWER noted five bare
`%{rows: _} =` matches reached only through guarded/2 or an outer rescue -- confirm that holds as
IDIOM, not just as safety), no dead code, no copy-paste from the very template this helper exists
to replace, and that a test-only module living in test/support/ genuinely does not need a
supervision-tree presence (compare test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex, which made the same call
deliberately and documents why).

CARRY-FORWARD, do not act on: SECURITY-REVIEWER recorded one non-blocking MINOR -- the failure
paths log raw Exception.message(exception) at tenant_fixture.ex:274 and :382, which is bounded
today (every query that can raise is tenant-scoped) but where a DBConnection.ConnectionError
message could include host:port. It recommended carrying this into ISS-0112/GH#366 rather than
expanding this run. ORCH will do that. Mention it only if you think that judgement is wrong.

CONSTRAINTS: you gate, you do not edit. On FAIL, name each gap specifically so rework is narrow.
Toolchain: plain `mix compile` only (Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 vs a 1.18.3-otp-27 pin, ISS-0106, filed
and not yours) -- no --warnings-as-errors, no `mix format`. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by
explicit filename, never `git add -A`. Note ORCH may have handoffs/orchestrator.log modified in
the working tree -- that file is ORCH's, leave it alone and fetch rather than pulling if a rebase
refuses.
acceptance_criteria: RULING 1 is given explicitly: whether implementing SS3.5's normative nil-degradation over SS3.2's literal boolean() is the correct resolution of the design's internal contradiction, and whether the resulting @type/@spec surface is coherent
RULING 2 is given explicitly: whether owning_test/0's :parent-chain process-dictionary walk is acceptable idiom for this test-only best-effort log field, or what it should do instead
RULING 3 is given explicitly: that excluding schema_migrations from tables_present is consistent and that SS3.3's oracle-rot guard still works against the implementation as written

RULING 4 is given explicitly: no scope creep -- one new test-only module, exactly two adopted modules, no production change, drop_schema!/1 retained for its SandboxPool caller, and none of ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113/0107 quietly absorbed

Ordinary idiom review of the new module is reported: naming, @spec accuracy against actual return shapes, the guarded/rescue structure as idiom, absence of dead code, and no supervision-tree need (compared against test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's documented precedent)
Decision-record consistency is checked -- no docs/migration/decisions/ record and no gate-approved design record is contradicted by the implementation
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated; on FAIL each gap is named specifically enough for narrow rework

result.summary: PASS. Idiom/scope/decision-record gate on the ISS-0109 implementation (git diff 70736d5..HEAD -- test/, plus docs/issues/ISS-0112.yaml which ORCH added mid-review). RULING 1 -- AGREED, and on a stronger ground than the one offered: implementing design 3.5's nil-degradation over 3.2's literal boolean() is correct, because taking 3.2 literally does not merely re-create ISS-0109's observed-vs-unobserved conflation, it VIOLATES INV-F-10. With schema_present? forced to boolean(), a capture whose information_schema.schemata query failed would report false, incompleteness_reasons/2 would emit 'schema is absent', and assert_schema_complete!/2 would turn a test with a perfectly good schema red -- exactly what INV-F-10 forbids. So 3.5 wins not by INV-F-4's precedence sentence alone but because the alternative breaks an invariant, while 3.5 breaks only 3.2's type line. The resulting surface is coherent: registration_present? and schema_present? are boolean() | nil with false=observed-absent / nil=not-observed, documented in both the @typedoc and the moduledoc; list fields keep [] (no type change needed); db_now, pg_backend_pid, provisioned_at and migrations_applied_at were already nil-able in 3.2. The one residual overlap -- provisioned_at/migrations_applied_at are nil both when the registration row is absent and when its query failed -- is disambiguated by the sibling registration_present? field, since all three come from one guard. ORCH should correct 3.2 to boolean() | nil for those two fields and keep the field NAMES unchanged (renaming would churn the design, the report format and the moduledoc for no gain; the tri-state is documented at both the type and the field). RULING 2 -- ACCEPTABLE AS WRITTEN, no change required. Process.info/2 is public OTP API; what is private is only the SHAPE stored under the ExUnit.Runner key, and current_test_of/1 pattern-matches that shape defensively with an '_other -> nil' fallback, so an ExUnit change degrades the field to "unknown" and cannot break a teardown. owning_test/0 additionally carries its own rescue, and Process.info(pid, :parent) raising on a pre-OTP-25 runtime lands in that same rescue. Reading the value at fixture-construction time and closing over it is the right call and is correctly justified in the comment (on_exit/1 callbacks do not run under the runner). Dropping the field was the available alternative and is the WRONG one: 3.6 names module+name as normative content of the line, and the only public alternative -- threading the ExUnit context in through opts -- would add a sixth normative opt and force every future ISS-0112 adopter to restructure its provisioned_tenant/0 to receive context, defeating the one-file-at-a-time property 3.1 exists to preserve. If this ever does cost maintenance, that opt is the fallback, not removal of the field. RULING 3 -- CONSISTENT, and the oracle-rot guard still works. tables_in/1 rejecting schema_migrations is symmetric with expected_tenant_tables/0 excluding it, so both-direction set equality holds with no filtering on TEST-DESIGNER's side, and tables_missing = expected -- tables_present is unaffected either way (an extra element in the left-hand list of -- is inert). One binding instruction for TEST-DESIGNER follows from this and must be carried into step 04: the 3.3 oracle-rot test MUST read the observed set from capture_schema_state/1's tables_present, NOT by querying information_schema.tables itself -- a raw catalog read returns schema_migrations and would fail the both-direction equality that 3.3 specifies as unfiltered. Non-blocking note: because schema_migrations is filtered out of tables_present, a wholly ABSENT schema_migrations table is invisible to check 2; it is still caught in practice, since a schema whose migrator bookkeeping never existed also has no tenant tables, so check 2 fires on those instead. RULING 4 -- NO SCOPE CREEP. Exactly one new test-only module (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, 630 lines); adoption in exactly the two modules 5 names; the other 39 copy-paste sites untouched; zero production change, so INV-F-2 holds (git diff --name-only over the range touches only handoffs/, the design doc's two ORCH label corrections, docs/issues/ISS-0112.yaml, and test/). drop_schema!/1 is retained in promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs at :93 and still called at :441 by the SandboxPool held-schema on_exit, with a comment explaining why it survives; it was correctly REMOVED from promotion_test.exs, which had no other caller. import Ecto.Query was correctly dropped from promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs (no remaining from/2) and correctly RETAINED in promotion_test.exs (still used at :391). None of the neighbouring issues is quietly absorbed: ISS-0110 (reaper min_age) and ISS-0111 (identity_migration_test bulk DELETE) are untouched; ISS-0112 gets only ORCH's carried_findings entry, not code; ISS-0113 is deliberately NOT fixed -- Sandbox.mode(:auto) is reproduced and :manual is not restored, per INV-F-6; ISS-0107 is untouched. Worth recording as a positive interaction rather than a finding: the new phase=teardown line's schema_present_before_drop=false is precisely the signal that would make an ISS-0110 occurrence attributable. ORDINARY IDIOM REVIEW. Naming is correct: bang functions raise (provisioned_tenant!/1, assert_schema_complete!/2), the non-bang capture returns a tagged tuple, expected_tenant_tables/0 reads as an oracle. Imports are scoped (only: [on_exit: 1], only: [from: 2]) rather than blanket. @specs match actual return shapes at all four public functions. The guarded/2 + per-field-degradation structure holds AS IDIOM, not merely as safety: the five bare '%{rows: _} =' matches (schema_present?/1, tables_in/1, applied_versions_in/1, db_now/0, pg_backend_pid/0) are each reached only through guarded/2 or do_capture/2's outer rescue, so asserting the expected shape and letting a mismatch raise into a guard is BETTER Elixir than defensive case branches that would have to invent a fallback value -- and inventing a fallback is exactly the observed/unobserved conflation 3.5 forbids. A blanket 'rescue _exception' is normally an Elixir anti-pattern; here it is the literal INV-F-4/INV-F-10 contract and is documented at every site, so it is justified rather than reflexive. The {:observed, value} tagging for fields whose legal value can itself be nil (registration) versus a bare nil sentinel for fields that cannot be nil (schema_present?) is a defensible asymmetry, though an explicit @typep observation(t) :: {:observed, t} | :unobserved would make the degraded case unrepresentable as a legal observed value instead of near-missing on nil. I am deliberately NOT filing that under docs/issues/ tagged type-safety: my charter conditions that on new transition logic, and filing an issue for a test helper's internal option type would itself be the queue noise this gate exists to prevent -- ISS-0112 is its natural home if ORCH wants it recorded. No dead code beyond one trivial item (MINOR-2 below): capture_schema_state/1, expected_tenant_tables/0 and opts[:teardown]=false are all unreferenced internally but are the 3.2/7 public surface TEST-DESIGNER builds on, not dead. No copy-paste from the template the helper replaces -- the hand-rolled bodies are genuinely deleted at both sites, not commented out or duplicated. SUPERVISION. Nothing collapsed process isolation: this is a plain module with no GenServer, no ETS, no Agent, no module-level mutable state and no spawn, so it needs no supervision-tree presence -- the identical call test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex makes deliberately and documents in its own moduledoc, and the shape 3/INV-F-1 require. Each test still gets its own real, separately-named Postgres schema; the fixture holds no cross-test state. The one shared-state mutation, Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto), is unchanged from today and is ISS-0113's, not this run's. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY. Checked docs/migration/decisions/0001-0007 and the two gate-approved design records in play. Nothing contradicted. 0006 (identity tables schema-per-tenant) is positively confirmed rather than merely not-violated: the oracle's 19 tables include users, groups, tenant_role and tokens INSIDE the tenant schema, which is 0006's conclusion, so a regression back to public-schema identity tables would now fail the oracle-rot test. 0003 is untouched -- raw Repo.query! here reads Postgres catalog metadata, which is outside 0003's business-table scope. 0001 (Plug/Bandit) is not in play. req022 lines 288-294's no-implicit-chaining invariant is respected: provision!/1 and replay!/1 sequence the two primitives explicitly and neither calls through the other (INV-F-3). 3.2's declared replay_migrations/2 versus the call site's replay_migrations(tenant_id) is not a discrepancy -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:238 defines it with a defaulted second argument. TOOLCHAIN EVIDENCE, run not assumed: 'MIX_ENV=test mix compile' exits 0 and produces _build/test/lib/letflow/ebin/Elixir.Letflow.TenantFixture.beam. A forced rebuild emits 28 warnings, all of them pre-existing set-theoretic-type warnings under lib/letflow/engine/ (ISS-0106 toolchain skew, filed, not this run's); grep over the compile output for tenant_fixture, promotion_test and promotion_assertion_rerun returns no matches, i.e. the three changed files compile clean. Per the dispatch I ran neither --warnings-as-errors nor mix format. CARRY-FORWARD JUDGEMENT. SECURITY-REVIEWER's exception-text MINOR was routed to ISS-0112 rather than expanded here; I agree, and ORCH has already landed it at d68b04b. MINOR-3 below belongs in the same place and should be decided together with it.

issues.description: DESIGN CORRECTION OWED (ruling 1, agreed): lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md section 3.2 types registration_present? and schema_present? as boolean(), which contradicts section 3.5's normative per-field nil-degradation and, taken literally, would violate INV-F-10 by failing a test whose schema is fine but whose catalog query failed. Section 3.2 should be corrected to 'boolean() | nil' for those two fields, with the field NAMES kept as-is. The implementation is correct; the design record is the artefact that needs the edit. Neither CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR pass caught this, which is itself worth a line in docs/anti-patterns.md: a design that declares one section normative over another must have its type table checked AGAINST that section, not only for internal well-formedness.

DEAD MAP KEY: do_capture/2 builds 'observed' with a :registration key that no caller ever reads -- incompleteness_reasons/2 consumes only :schema, :tables and :versions. Harmless and arguably a coherent completion of the observation map, but it is unused state. Either drop it or note in a comment that it exists for symmetry/future use.

DIAGNOSTIC REGRESSION vs. THE SIBLING PRECEDENT, for ISS-0112 to decide alongside SECURITY-REVIEWER's carried exception-text MINOR (same two lines): tenant_fixture.ex:274 and :382 log Exception.message(exception), whereas test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:92 and :113 log Exception.format(:error, exception, __STACKTRACE__). For a module whose entire purpose is making the next failure attributable, dropping the stacktrace on a capture failure loses the most attributable part. The two findings pull in opposite directions -- one wants less text, one wants more -- so they must be decided together, in ISS-0112, not separately.

EXIT vs RAISE, non-blocking and consistent with precedent: guarded/2 and do_capture/2's outer net use 'rescue', which does not catch process exits. A DBConnection owner-death exit during capture would therefore escape capture_schema_state/1, which INV-F-4's letter ('never raises') survives but whose spirit it does not. test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex makes exactly the same rescue-only choice, so this is the established, gate-approved level of defence for test/support/ rather than a new gap. If it is ever tightened to try/catch on :exit, tighten both modules together -- ISS-0112 again.

SPEC/ARITY NIT (repo-wide pattern, not introduced here): provisioned_tenant!/1 and assert_schema_complete!/2 each declare a default argument, generating a lower arity that the single @spec does not cover, so provisioned_tenant!/0 and assert_schema_complete!/1 are unspecced. Cosmetic; dialyzer does not warn because the max-arity function exists.

STYLE NITS, none worth rework on their own: (a) parent_chain(self(), 4) uses a bare magic depth with no named constant or comment justifying 4; (b) Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1 is called fully qualified although the module opens with an alias block for Repo/Tenant/TenantProvisioning/Registration; (c) current_test_of/1 matches on a bare __struct__ map rather than %ExUnit.Test{} -- defensible as deliberate decoupling from a private struct, but it deserves the one-line comment it currently lacks, since it otherwise reads as an accident.

result.next_action: Proceed to WF-03 step 04 (TEST-DESIGNER). Two things must ride along in that dispatch. (1) BINDING, from ruling 3: the section 3.3 oracle-rot test must take its observed table set from Letflow.TenantFixture.capture_schema_state/1's tables_present and assert both-direction set equality against expected_tenant_tables/0 -- it must NOT query information_schema.tables directly, because a raw catalog read includes schema_migrations and would fail the unfiltered equality section 3.3 specifies. (2) Section 7's fail-first tests are what make opts[:teardown]=false non-dead; TEST-DESIGNER owns them. Separately, ORCH should apply MINOR-1's design correction to section 3.2 (boolean() | nil, field names unchanged) so the record and the code agree before this branch merges, and consider MINOR-1's closing anti-patterns.md line about validating a design's type table against whichever section it declares normative. MINOR-2 through MINOR-6 are all non-blocking; MINOR-3 and MINOR-4 belong in ISS-0112 alongside SECURITY-REVIEWER's already-carried exception-text finding, and the rest can ride ISS-0112 or be ignored. No rework is required of ELIXIR-DEV.
